# Clause words

Every paragraph in this section breaks before a clause word.
The break is kept because the word starts a clause of its own.

The cache is written to the build directory
and the next build reads it back.

The first build is slow on every agent
but the later builds reuse the cache.

Pass the path on the command line
or set it in the configuration file.

The tool never deletes the source files
nor does it overwrite the backups.

The cache holds every compiled module
yet it stays under one gigabyte.

The lock file pins every dependency
so two machines build the same thing.

The formatter skips generated files
because nobody edits them by hand.

The old flag still works for now
since some scripts depend on it.

The report lists every warning
although most of them are harmless.

The check runs on every commit
though it only fails on errors.

The server keeps serving old requests
while the new version starts up.

The debug build keeps every symbol
whereas the release build strips them.

The command prints a short summary
if the verbose flag is not set.

The upload is retried three times
unless the server rejects the token.

The watcher keeps polling the directory
until the user stops it.

The migration rewrites every row
without locking the whole table.

The index is rebuilt from scratch
when the schema version changes.

The log file is rotated automatically
whenever it grows past the limit.

The files are copied to the target directory
where the installer picks them up.

The temporary files are removed
after the archive has been written.

The configuration is validated in full
before any file is touched.

The parser reports the first error
rather than guessing what was meant.

The tool prints the planned changes
instead of writing them to disk.

Every file in the directory is scanned
except the hidden ones.

The script builds the release archive
then uploads it to the server.

The value must be a positive number
otherwise the default is used.

The first run downloads every package
however the later runs work offline.

The test suite runs in parallel
therefore each test uses its own directory.

The cache key includes the compiler version

The tool accepts several archive formats
e.g. zip, tar, and seven zip.

The command only reads the working tree

## Connectors of several words

The option takes any glob pattern
for example a star followed by an extension.

The formatter understands common markup
such as emphasis and inline code.

The archive contains the binaries, and it ships the docs
as well as the license files.

The cache is reused, even by every later build

The deploy step stops, and the release is held back
as soon as one of the tests fails.

The renamed file is kept, and it is treated
as if it had always had the new name.

The old option is deprecated, but it keeps working
as though nothing had changed.

The index is sorted by name
in order to make lookups fast.

## Relative pronouns without an earlier comma

A bare relative pronoun or "as" is kept when nothing earlier on the line could take the break.

The tool writes a report file
which the CI job uploads afterwards.

The request marks the archive entry
as a favourite of the signed in reader.

## Relative pronouns after an earlier comma

The break moves to the comma when that reads better and keeps the lines balanced.

Build the container image with the layer cache from the previous build of the same branch,
